title: workload-presets-and-spreadsheet-template-for-cost-sweeps-draft
content:
Purpose: quick, pragmatic set of recommended starting presets and a spreadsheet template for running cost-performance sweeps across batching, caching, and quantization. Intention is to standardize experiments so teams can reproduce cost deltas and pick safe defaults when onboarding workloads to Redwood Optimize.

Context and assumptions:
- This is a product-facing draft for engineering and solutions to run quick cost sweeps. Not a runtime spec.
- Cost numbers assume the GPU pool has quoted hourly price (variable by cloud region). The spreadsheet converts GPU-hour to token/unit cost so product can compare options.
- We assume support for at least: full fp16, int8-like quant (lossy), and 4-bit qconfigs for modern LLMs. If a model lacks q4 support, note and revert to int8.
- KV/prefix cache: we target conversational workloads where prefix reuse is common. For low-reuse workloads, caching is disabled.

Workload profile presets (human-readable):
1) latency-sensitive chat (LS-chat)
   - description: interactive chat with average user patience < 200ms for first token. Typical request length 20–120 tokens, with prefix reuse across turns.
   - recommended starting presets: batch_size = 1; concurrent_req_limit = 100 (client-side throttling); pref_kv_cache = enabled; cache_retention = 1200s; quantization = q4_0 (if verified) else fp16; dynamic_batch_timeout = 10ms; fallback_model = smaller fp16 replica for tail-latency.

2) high-throughput embeddings (HT-embed)
   - description: batching many short requests (<= 256 tokens) for embeddings or vectorization jobs. Latency less critical, throughput matters.
   - recommended starting presets: batch_size = 256 (or server max); concurrent_req_limit = 2000; pref_kv_cache = disabled (no prefix reuse); quantization = int8 (if embeddings preserved), else fp16; dynamic_batch_timeout = 50ms; autoscale_policy = aggressive-burst.

3) long-context summarization (LC-sum)
   - description: single large requests (2k–32k tokens) with heavy KV cache pressure and long decoding. Often smaller QPS.
   - recommended starting presets: batch_size = 1 or small (<=8) depending on mem; concurrent_req_limit = 20; pref_kv_cache = partial (store recent 3K tokens as prefix); quantization = fp16 preferred for quality; if quantized, validate at 2–3 eval prompts; dynamic_batch_timeout = 100ms; memory_margin = +20% to avoid OOM.

4) reranking / scoring (RR-score)
   - description: high qps scoring of short candidate texts (5–50 tokens) where per-token cost dominates.
   - recommended starting presets: batch_size = 64–128; concurrent_req_limit = 1000; pref_kv_cache = disabled; quantization = int8 or q4 with accuracy checks; dynamic_batch_timeout = 20ms; prefer longer batching window for micro-bursts.

Spreadsheet template (column names and formulas so users can paste into a sheet):
- Columns (one per column header):
  - scenario_name
  - model
  - gpu_hourly_price_usd
  - quantization
  - batch_size
  - avg_input_tokens_per_request
  - avg_output_tokens_per_request
  - avg_tokens_per_request (formula) = "=avg_input_tokens_per_request + avg_output_tokens_per_request"
  - measured_latency_ms_per_request
  - requests_per_second (rps)
  - effective_throughput_tokens_per_second (formula) = "=requests_per_second * avg_tokens_per_request"
  - gpu_utilization_pct (measured)
  - tokens_per_gpu_second_effective (formula) = "=effective_throughput_tokens_per_second / (gpu_utilization_pct/100)"
  - cost_per_gpu_second_usd (formula) = "=gpu_hourly_price_usd/3600"
  - cost_per_token_usd (formula) = "=cost_per_gpu_second_usd / tokens_per_gpu_second_effective"
  - est_monthly_cost_usd (formula) = "=cost_per_token_usd * projected_monthly_tokens"
  - notes

Example quick numbers (fill these into the spreadsheet to sanity-check):
- Example LS-chat baseline: model=X, gpu_hourly_price_usd=8.0, quantization=fp16, batch_size=1, avg_tokens=60, measured_latency_ms_per_request=150, rps=40, gpu_utilization_pct=35 => tokens_per_gpu_second_effective approx = (40*60)/(0.35) = 6885 t/s; cost_per_token ~ (8/3600)/6885 ≈ 3.2e-7 USD/token.
- If applying q4_0 and measured tokens/sec improves 1.7x (faster kernels), cost_per_token drops roughly 1.7x. If caching reduces output tokens by 15% across sessions, another 15% reduction. Combined tweaks compound.

How to run a sweep (practical steps):
1) pick a 24–72h representative trace or synthetic traffic pattern (include user think-time for chat flows).
2) pick 3–4 quantization settings (fp16, int8, q4_0, q4_1) depending on model support.
3) pick batch_size values: [1, 4, 16, 64, 256] but prune by memory for long-context models.
4) pick cache policies: disabled, prefix-only (N tokens), full-session.
5) instrument: latency p50/p95, tokens/s, GPU utilization, model-quality A/B metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim) or domain-specific metric.
6) run each combination for at least 1 hour under stable load, capture steady-state windows.
7) populate the spreadsheet and compute cost_per_token delta vs baseline.

Recommended acceptance criteria for a preset: change must not degrade quality metric by >1% absolute (or business-approved threshold) and must reduce cost_per_token by >=10% for it to be considered as a default. For latency-sensitive workloads, max increase in p50 first-token latency <= 10ms unless offset by fallbacks.

Operational guardrails and quick checks:
- Always run a small regression suite (5–10 golden prompts) pre/post quantization and caching change. Put the golden prompts into the spreadsheet as a separate tab.
- If KV cache is enabled, monitor cache hit rate and memory pressure. If hit rate < 20% after 48h on chat workload, revert cache policy.
- For QConfigs: keep a mapping table (model -> validated qconfigs). Add a column in the spreadsheet for validation_status and validation_date.

Suggested default profiles (machine-readable names teams can reference):
- redwood:ls-chat-default (maps to LS-chat presets above)
- redwood:ht-embed-default
- redwood:lc-sum-safe
- redwood:rr-score-highbatch

Evaluation checklist before rolling to prod:
- run 48h sweep on a staging dedicated pool
- verify cost spreadsheet and expected savings are repeatable across 3 runs
- run regression prompts and sanity-check embedding similarity/latency
- create a rollback policy (automated fallback to fp16 model/version)

Open questions / items for engineering:
- can runtime surface per-batch/kernel-level token throughput quickly to reduce measurement noise? (ticket: JIRA-OPT-1127)
- can we expose a simple knob for dynamic_batch_timeout at route level in the console?
- confirm which q4 variants are supported for the most common models and create a whitelist file in repo.

Next steps (owner: Maya Chen):
- convert the spreadsheet skeleton into a Google Sheet template and link from Optimize docs (due: 2026-03-05)
- run two example sweeps (chat and embeddings) with solutions-eng (due: 2026-03-18)
- collect feedback and finalize recommended presets for stable release (target: Q2 2026)

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally pragmatic and conservative. The point is not to squeeze every percent of performance but to provide reproducible experiments and safe defaults that reduce immediate unit cost for customers. Feedback welcome on the acceptance thresholds and the sample spreadsheet formulas.

Quick references and links: see linked_artifacts above.

-- Maya
